newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Chem, Mitsui Toatsu say to merge units.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Chem, Mitsui Toatsu say to merge units.

text.p: Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd and Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc said on Monday that they will merge their polystyrene units by October.
The firms said in a statement that they plan to set up a new firm on October 1 to take over the polystyrene operations of the two units.
It said the output of the combined units would be 242,000 tonnes a year. This would make the new firm Japan's second largest polystyrene producer after Asahi Chemical Industry Co Ltd.
They said the new firm would be capitalised at two billion yen, to be shouldered equally by the two firms.

Mitsui Toatsu plans to merge with Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd in October to become Mitsui Chemicals Inc, which will be the second largest chemical manufacturer in Japan after Mitsubishi Chemical Corp.
Sumitomo Chemical and Mitsui Toatsu said the combined polystyrene unit would aim for initial sales of 25 billion yen a year.
It will employ about 100 people in the manufacture and sale of polystyrene and related projects.
The firms said they had not yet decided upon a name for the new company.
